High level asks from HealthSync:

- Who on Redwood will run the smoke validation and who needs to accept results?
- Evidence artifacts for security/compliance (audit logs, data retention config).

Can you share a single one-sheet that lists exit gates and acceptance tests so we can route internally?

Thanks,

HealthSync

Subject: Pilot verification and go/no-go ledger for HealthSync integration

Oliver — thanks for outlining this. I've drafted a concise MAP and verification roster attached; below are the core exit gates and the acceptance tests we propose for the pilot (aimed at an 8-week evaluation window).

Proposed exit gates (all must be met for a go):
1) Functional correctness: end-to-end flows for the 3 primary use cases (clinical summaries, triage routing, patient Q&A) show >= 95% pass rate on the test suite (see test IDs in acceptance-tests.yaml).
2) Latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for single-turn requests and <= 400ms for multi-turn with 2k-token contexts under pilot traffic profile.
3) Quality threshold: automated evaluation (BLEU/ROUGE-style surrogate + human spot-check) average relevance score >= 0.78 and no catastrophic hallucination in critical fields in >98% of sampled cases.
4) Reliability: 99.5% availability during business hours (US ET) and graceful fallback to smaller model variant without data leakage when capacity constrained.
5) Security/compliance: audit log retention, KMS key access logs, and a SOC2 evidence packet delivered to procurement.

Acceptance tests and owners (high-level):
- Smoke validation (owner: Redwood SRE / Jonas Weber): run synthetic traffic harness and verify latency/SLA targets.
- Accuracy spot-checks (owner: HealthSync ops / Oliver): review 200-sample human annotations; Redwood provides sample export and tooling.
- Data handling audit (owner: Redwood security / Karthik Iyer): provide config, retention policy, and access logs package.
- Failover test (owner: Redwood runtime / Marissa): trigger capacity fallback and validate no PII flows to fallback variant.

Deliverables and timeline (week-of dates):
- Week 0 (Oct 25): Finalize MAP and sign-off on test set.
- Week 1–2 (Nov 1–Nov 14): Deploy pilot infra, run baseline smoke tests.
- Week 3–5 (Nov 15–Dec 5): Evaluation window — accuracy + load/latency runs.
- Week 6 (Dec 6–Dec 12): Review results, decision meeting, and procurement sign-off.

I'll attach the MAP workbook and the acceptance-tests.yaml for your folks to review. If this aligns, can we get a procurement lead and a legal contact to loop in so we can pin the 30-day procurement window?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example

Attachments: "MAP-HealthSync-v1.xlsx", "acceptance-tests.yaml"

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>, Oliver Chen <oliver@healthsync.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot verification and go/no-go ledger for HealthSync integration

Marissa — this looks like a solid starting point. Two quick technical clarifications to ensure the acceptance tests are actionable:

1) Latency SLOs: we should specify request size buckets (short <512 tokens, medium 512–2048, long >2048) and capture p50/p95/p99. For pilot acceptance we'll gate on p95 but capture p99 for risk. Proposal: short p95 <= 120ms, medium p95 <= 200ms, long p95 <= 380ms.

2) Quality eval: the automated surrogate we run is a prompt-based entailment check plus a domain-specific token blacklist for hallucination. We should include a small seed of edge-case prompts (20) that HealthSync flags as critical — they must pass manual review.

Also recommending we add a rollback trigger: if during evaluation we see a >3% rate of hallucination in critical fields across any 24h window, we automatically pause new requests and convene incident review.

I'll own the security evidence bundle (draft will be in the Drive link). Jonas, can you confirm SRE will run a load harness during Week 2?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Product Security
